_readme: Lists every image the game loads. Replace any PNG in assets/sprites with your own art of the SAME size and layout, or change the numbers here to match your new art. See ART_GUIDE.md.

greyhound.notes: Made from Dave's grey Copilot dog (assets/source/greyhound_grey_designer.png) by tools/import_grey_greyhound.py: one row per coat colour, 8-frame gallop, no jacket.

jacket.notes: Jackets with numbers, worked out from the dog's outline in each frame by the same tool, so they line up exactly with greyhound_coats_run.png.

greyhoundPainted.notes: Dave's sheet, converted by tools/import_greyhound_sheet.py from assets/source/greyhound_sheet_designer.png. One row per trap with the jacket painted on, 12-frame gallop. To go back to the placeholder art, swap this entry for 'greyhoundPlaceholder' below and rename it 'greyhound'.

greyhoundPlaceholder.notes: One row per coat colour, 8-frame gallop cycle left to right, dog running to the right. anchor = the point placed on the dog's position (centre of body, at paw level).

jacketPlaceholder.notes: Racing jackets drawn on their own, on a transparent background, lined up exactly over the matching greyhound frame.

traps.notes: Frame 0 closed, frame 1 open. Trap 1 at the bottom (nearest the rail), trap 6 at the top.

background._notes: Layers drawn back to front. 'y' is the top edge on the 640x240 race screen. 'scroll' is how fast it moves with the camera (1 = with the track, 0 = fixed). 'repeat' tiles the image sideways.

layers.notes: The grandstands. Each track picks its stands from 'stands' below (see 'stands' in data/tracks.json); this file is only used for a track that doesn't name any. Stands are drawn side by side with their bottom edge at 'bottom', and 'fill' is painted behind them from the bottom of the sky down. The placeholder is sprites/stand.png (y 26).
Dave's Copilot advert boards in one strip, made by tools/import_background.py. The placeholder is sprites/hoardings.png (y 88).

stands._notes: Made from Dave's sheet (assets/source/stands_sheet_designer.png) by tools/import_background.py. Any size works: each stand is drawn with its bottom edge on the stand layer's 'bottom'. Keep them under about 88 pixels tall so they fit under the top of the screen.
